label: <DEL> step, first output is h/i/d/v (or short sequence)
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (99% of activation mass at t == L, where the model starts by outputting original token 0); it never fires in the copy phase, and only weakly on a few late original-phase steps (o/z inputs). Among delimiter steps (12.6% active) the magnitude is graded by two factors: the identity of the first original token, the one about to be output (h, i, d, v have rates of 5-10x baseline and hold about 68% of mass; x, y, m, b, s, l are next), and shortness of the sequence (L=3-5 has much higher rates; L>=8 is rare). The final tokens before <DEL> (p, o, q, g) increase it a little more. The predicate combines these thresholds, so precision and recall are both around 0.6: the response looks like an additive score more than a clean category.
